correctness.rationale: For each vacant length n>=3 interval, the loss equation has n-2 internal triple starts and exactly four starts crossing its boundaries; all four extensions have lengths n+1 or n+2. The candidate E_{i,n}=exp(-t sum_{j=i}^{i+n-3}r_j) u_parity(i)u_parity(i+n-1) with the two displayed u0,u1 ODEs satisfies each equation. The bounded linear hierarchy uniqueness follows from Duhamel/Gronwall after factoring negative diagonal terms; the probability solution is bounded, so the ansatz is the correct infinite-lattice vacancy probability. Successful triple arrival rates are a exp(-at)u0^2 and b exp(-bt)u1^2; counting two even/one odd, or reverse, yields C0=2J0+J1, C1=J0+2J1. For b=eps->0, on compact fast time u0,u1->exp(-(1-e^{-at})), yielding J0->(1-e^-2)/2. Uniform tail bounds give u1(s/eps)->e^-1 for each s>0; changing variable v=eps t and dominated convergence gives J1(s/eps)->e^-2(1-e^-s), including s=infinity. This proves exact singular jump in mean 3e^-2/2 between b downarrow0 after jamming vs b=0 initially. Independently checked 44 vacancy hierarchy equations at each of four times for rates (1,1),(1,.2),(2,3),(.1,1) with fresh SciPy ODE integration and independently formed residuals.
residual_risks: The s>0 pointwise slow-scale limit is not asserted uniform through s=0; finite numerical tolerance cannot prove the infinite-volume hierarchy.

value.rationale: Parity-dependent deposition rates are a natural kinetic perturbation in irreversible hard-segment adsorption. The complete finite-time two-component infinite-volume closure is an exact tractable inhomogeneous RSA model; the slow b->0 limit yields a noncommutation of jamming and parameter limit with an explicit nonzero coverage jump 3e^-2/2 and a universal exponential slow-time profile. Both the object and invariant are physically/mathematically motivated, and the result is not a finite simulation or a trivial homogeneous parameter substitution.
